questions.q: Which of these is a drift-based trigger for retraining, as distinct from a performance-based one?
options: Retraining every Sunday night regardless of conditions
Retraining because a monitored accuracy metric has already dropped below a threshold
Retraining because input feature distributions have statistically shifted, detected before a lagging performance metric necessarily shows damage
Retraining whenever a new engineer joins the team
questions.explain: Drift-based triggers react to a statistical shift in inputs or predictions, often catching a problem earlier than a performance metric that lags behind.

questions.q: In the PSI-based drift check example, why does the threshold matter being fixed and documented rather than decided fresh each time?
options: Because PSI cannot be calculated without a fixed threshold
A consistent, documented threshold avoids noisy, inconsistent decisions about when a shift is 'significant enough' to act on
Because Airflow requires all thresholds to be hardcoded constants
There is no benefit — a fresh judgment call each time is actually preferred
questions.explain: A fixed, documented threshold (such as PSI > 0.2) keeps drift-triggered retraining consistent instead of relying on a different judgment call each time it runs.

questions.q: Why is the quality gate described as the single most important line in the retraining pipeline?
options: Because it is the only line that logs to MLflow
Because a pipeline that promotes every newly retrained model unconditionally can silently degrade production the moment one bad run finishes without error
Because it is required by Airflow's syntax
Because without it, the pipeline would fail to compile
questions.explain: Without a quality gate requiring the candidate to actually beat the champion, automated retraining becomes an unsupervised way to push a worse model into production.

questions.q: What should happen when a retrained candidate model fails the quality gate?
options: It should be promoted anyway, since retraining already happened
The pipeline should do nothing to production and alert a human, rather than promoting or silently giving up
The entire registry should be deleted
The champion alias should be removed entirely with no replacement
questions.explain: A failed gate means production stays on the current champion; the correct response is to alert a human rather than promote a candidate that didn't clear the bar.

questions.q: What did the manual, pre-automation version of 'retraining' typically depend on, according to this lesson?
options: A fully automated system with no human involvement at all
A person noticing something looked off, pulling data by hand, eyeballing a metric, and manually copying a file
A quality gate identical to the automated one described in this lesson
Weights & Biases' Model Registry exclusively
questions.explain: Before building this pipeline, retraining relied entirely on a person remembering to notice, pull data, evaluate, and move files by hand — exactly the dependency this chapter's automation removes.
